core_obligations: Prove that in the situation of the dilatations theorem, f : X' -> X is quasi-compact if and only if g : W -> X_{/T} is quasi-compact
proof_roadmap: One direction is quoted from lemma-quasi-compact-gives-quasi-compact.

Conversely, base change to an etale affine covering {X_i -> X} reduces to X affine; the formal base changes W_i x_{X_{/T}} (X_i)_{/T} -> (X_i)_{/T} are quasi-compact, and the functoriality of the completion functor reduces further to the affine case.

For X affine: a surjective etale V = coprod V_j -> X' gives a surjective etale V_{/T} -> W; quasi-compactness of W yields a finite J' with coprod_{J'} (V_j)_{/T} -> W surjective, and since |X'| = |U| union |W_red| the finite union U plus coprod_{J'} V_j covers X', so X' is quasi-compact.
difficulty_reason: H3: an etale-local reduction and a finite-subcover argument on the formal fibre, using the topological decomposition of the dilatation.
